heldout_policy: All sections use held-out test rows only. Diagnostic complete-dataset rows that include training data are excluded from this report.

experiment_definitions.definition: Trained on the main PhiUSIIL dataset and tested on the main PhiUSIIL held-out 20 percent test split.
Trained on the main PhiUSIIL dataset and tested against external datasets.
Trained on the remaining datasets and tested against other datasets, not the dataset used for training.
Trained on each single dataset and tested against the combined held-out test dataset.
Trained on the combined dataset and tested against the combined held-out test dataset.
Saved models tested on 20 normal websites and 20 held-out phishing URLs to check practical false positives and missed phishing.
Google trailing-slash brittleness check, comparing predictions for https://www.google.com and https://www.google.com/.

experiments.title: Each model trained and tested on the main PhiUSIIL dataset
experiments.purpose: 80/20 split on PhiUSIIL only. This is the same-source baseline.
plain_english_summary: Winner: XGBoost is ranked first because it has the highest F1 in this experiment: 0.9951. F1 is the main score here because it balances catching phishing URLs with avoiding false phishing alarms.
For this winner, precision is 0.9990, recall is 0.9912, and accuracy is 0.9958. Precision means how trustworthy its phishing warnings are; recall means how many real phishing URLs it catches.
Runner-up: Random Forest is second with F1 0.9948. The gap from the winner is 0.0003, so the result is almost tied and should be treated as very close.
The best exact row for the winner is trained on PhiUSIIL main and tested on PhiUSIIL held-out test, with F1 0.9951.
Measurement note: precision and recall are fairly balanced, so the F1 score is a reasonable single summary for this section.
Conclusion: for Experiment 1a, XGBoost gives the strongest current held-out evidence under this training/testing setup.

experiments.title: Main-trained models tested against external datasets
experiments.purpose: Models are trained on PhiUSIIL and tested on external held-out datasets.
plain_english_summary: Winner: Linear SVM is ranked first because it has the highest mean F1 in this experiment: 0.8336. F1 is the main score here because it balances catching phishing URLs with avoiding false phishing alarms.
For this winner, precision is 0.7789, recall is 0.9135, and accuracy is 0.7947. Precision means how trustworthy its phishing warnings are; recall means how many real phishing URLs it catches.
Runner-up: XGBoost is second with mean F1 0.8313. The gap from the winner is 0.0023, so the runner-up is close, so both models are competitive here.
Robustness check: the winner's worst F1 in this section is 0.6723. The drop from mean F1 is 0.1613, which shows how much its performance changes across the tested datasets in this experiment.

Best single held-out row: XGBoost has the highest individual F1 result, 0.9964, when trained on PhiUSIIL main and tested on LegitPhish. The section winner is still Linear SVM because the section ranking is based on overall model performance across the experiment rows.
Measurement note: recall is higher than precision by 0.1346, so this model catches more phishing URLs but may create more false phishing alarms.
Conclusion: for Experiment 1b, Linear SVM gives the strongest current held-out evidence under this training/testing setup.

experiments.title: External-trained models tested against other single-source datasets
experiments.purpose: Models are trained on LegitPhish or PhishStorm, then tested on different held-out datasets only.
plain_english_summary: Winner: XGBoost is ranked first because it has the highest mean F1 in this experiment: 0.7592. F1 is the main score here because it balances catching phishing URLs with avoiding false phishing alarms.
For this winner, precision is 0.6871, recall is 0.9029, and accuracy is 0.6887. Precision means how trustworthy its phishing warnings are; recall means how many real phishing URLs it catches.
Runner-up: Logistic Regression is second with mean F1 0.7493. The gap from the winner is 0.0099, so the runner-up is close, so both models are competitive here.
Robustness check: the winner's worst F1 in this section is 0.6613. The drop from mean F1 is 0.0979, which shows how much its performance changes across the tested datasets in this experiment.

Best single held-out row: Random Forest has the highest individual F1 result, 0.9712, when trained on LegitPhish and tested on PhiUSIIL held-out test. The section winner is still XGBoost because the section ranking is based on overall model performance across the experiment rows.
Measurement note: recall is higher than precision by 0.2158, so this model catches more phishing URLs but may create more false phishing alarms.
Conclusion: for Experiment 1c, XGBoost gives the strongest current held-out evidence under this training/testing setup.

experiments.title: Single-source models tested against the combined held-out dataset
experiments.purpose: Each model is trained on one source dataset and tested on the mixed combined test set.
plain_english_summary: Winner: XGBoost is ranked first because it has the highest mean F1 in this experiment: 0.8360. F1 is the main score here because it balances catching phishing URLs with avoiding false phishing alarms.
For this winner, precision is 0.7575, recall is 0.9345, and accuracy is 0.8088. Precision means how trustworthy its phishing warnings are; recall means how many real phishing URLs it catches.
Runner-up: Random Forest is second with mean F1 0.8238. The gap from the winner is 0.0122, so the winner has a noticeable advantage in this section.
Robustness check: the winner's worst F1 in this section is 0.7540. The drop from mean F1 is 0.0820, which shows how much its performance changes across the tested datasets in this experiment.

Best single held-out row: Linear SVM has the highest individual F1 result, 0.9070, when trained on PhiUSIIL main and tested on Combined held-out test. The section winner is still XGBoost because the section ranking is based on overall model performance across the experiment rows.
Measurement note: recall is higher than precision by 0.1770, so this model catches more phishing URLs but may create more false phishing alarms.
Conclusion: for Experiment 2a, XGBoost gives the strongest current held-out evidence under this training/testing setup.

experiments.title: Combined-trained models tested against the combined held-out dataset
experiments.purpose: Each model is trained on the combined training dataset and tested on the combined held-out test set.
plain_english_summary: Winner: XGBoost is ranked first because it has the highest F1 in this experiment: 0.9780. F1 is the main score here because it balances catching phishing URLs with avoiding false phishing alarms.
For this winner, precision is 0.9850, recall is 0.9711, and accuracy is 0.9748. Precision means how trustworthy its phishing warnings are; recall means how many real phishing URLs it catches.
Runner-up: Random Forest is second with F1 0.9779. The gap from the winner is 0.0001, so the result is almost tied and should be treated as very close.
The best exact row for the winner is trained on Combined dataset and tested on Combined held-out test, with F1 0.9780.
Measurement note: precision and recall are fairly balanced, so the F1 score is a reasonable single summary for this section.
Conclusion: for Experiment 2b, XGBoost gives the strongest current held-out evidence under this training/testing setup.

backend_recommendation.title: Combined-trained models tested against the combined held-out dataset
backend_recommendation.why: This is the most backend-like scenario: combined training data and a separate combined held-out test set.

experiment_winners.title: Each model trained and tested on the main PhiUSIIL dataset
experiment_winners.why: Best same-source PhiUSIIL baseline on the 80/20 test split.

experiment_winners.title: Main-trained models tested against external datasets
experiment_winners.why: Best average external-test performance for models trained only on PhiUSIIL. Best single row: XGBoost trained on PhiUSIIL main, tested on LegitPhish.

experiment_winners.title: External-trained models tested against other single-source datasets
experiment_winners.why: Best average cross-source result when the test dataset is not the training dataset. Best single row: Random Forest trained on LegitPhish, tested on PhiUSIIL held-out test.

experiment_winners.title: Single-source models tested against the combined held-out dataset
experiment_winners.why: Best average single-source training result on the mixed combined held-out test set. Best single row: Linear SVM trained on PhiUSIIL main, tested on Combined held-out test.

experiment_winners.title: Combined-trained models tested against the combined held-out dataset
experiment_winners.why: This is the most backend-like scenario: combined training data and a separate combined held-out test set.

decision_summary.method: Models are ranked primarily by phishing F1. Recall, precision, and accuracy are used as supporting evidence. For experiments with more than one test row, the report uses mean F1 and also shows worst F1 so a model is not judged from one lucky result only.

sanity_probe.title: 40-URL real-world sanity probe
sanity_probe.purpose: Saved models are tested on 20 normal websites and 20 held-out phishing URLs to inspect false positives and missed phishing.
